For rational $0<e\le\delta\le1/2$, the intended OP1A construction returns an odd real polynomial $p$ of degree $O(\delta^{-1}\log(1/e))$ satisfying $|p(x)|\le1$ on $[-1,1]$, $p(0)=0$, and
$$\sup_{x\in[\delta,1]}\left|p(x)-\frac{\delta}{2x}\right|\le e.$$
For a normalized block $\bar A=A/\alpha$ whose supported singular values lie in $\{0\}\cup[\delta,1]$, this gives the singular-space approximation $p^{\rm SV}(\bar A^\dagger)\approx(\delta/2)\bar A^+=(\gamma/2)A^+$ on the supported input, where $\delta=\gamma/\alpha$.

In the block-encoded QLSP model, let $|b\rangle$ be the normalized codomain input, let $\|A\|_{\rm op}\le\alpha$, and suppose $|b\rangle=\sum_{j=1}^r\beta_j|u_j\rangle$ is supported on positive singular values $\sigma_j\ge\gamma>0$. Then
$$\frac{(\delta/2)\bar A^+|b\rangle}{\|(\delta/2)\bar A^+|b\rangle\|}=\frac{A^+|b\rangle}{\|A^+|b\rangle\|},\qquad \left\|(\delta/2)\bar A^+|b\rangle\right\|^2\ge\frac{\delta^2}{4},\qquad \delta=\gamma/\alpha,\quad\bar A=A/\alpha.$$
In particular the ideal inverse-branch success probability is positive and has the stated crude lower bound.
The coherent $\Phi$/$-\Phi$ branch then has compressed block $p^{\mathrm{SV}}(A)$; for a supplied uniform scalar error $\eta$, its block differs from $p^{\mathrm{SV}}(A)$ by at most $\eta$.

For degree $d\ge0$, one un-controlled QSVT sequence makes exactly $d$ signal calls: $\lceil d/2\rceil$ calls to $U$ and $\lfloor d/2\rfloor$ calls to $U^*$, beginning with $U$ when $d>0$. It applies exactly $d+1$ projector-phase operations, with $\lceil(d+1)/2\rceil$ about $\Pi_R$ and $\lfloor(d+1)/2\rfloor$ about $\Pi_L$. By [[thm-qa-24-projector-phase-implementation]], each phase operation uses two controlled calls to the corresponding reflection and one variable one-qubit phase rotation, plus a constant number of one-qubit gates. A coherent control of one sequence against the identity requires no controlled signal call when $d$ is even and one controlled signal call when $d$ is odd. Selecting between the two phase lists $\Phi$ and $-\Phi$ uses the same unconditioned signal list in both branches and controls only the phase rotations. Phase generation, inverse access, and finite-gate compilation retain their separately declared costs. At $d=0$ there is no signal or controlled-signal call.

For $a>0$, the expected total number of calls made by [[alg-qa-12-unknown-amplitude-search]] to $A$, $A^\dagger$, the good and zero-input phase operations, and any one-call verifier is $\Theta(a^{-1/2})$. Define the root-mean-square stopping time
$$T_{\rm av}:=\left(\sum_{i=1}^m p_i t_i^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
Let $p_{\rm succ}$ be the total Born probability of the good-output subspace. When $p_{\rm succ}>0$, the good output means the normalized conditional state of the declared good projector; it is defined only on that positive-probability branch. The mean stopping time $\sum_i p_i t_i$ is a different quantity and is not substituted for $T_{\rm av}$.

Let a finite coherent variable-time algorithm satisfy [[def-qa-27-variable-time-model]], have $m$ stopping times and $T_{\max}\ge1$, RMS stopping time $T_{\rm av}$, and good-output probability $p_{\rm succ}>0$. Under the reversible stopping semantics of the model and supplied inverse and coherent access to every operation used, Ambainis' variable-time amplification procedure produces the conditional good state with success probability at least $1/2$ using time
$$O\!\left(T_{\max}\sqrt{\ln L_T}+\frac{T_{\rm av}}{\sqrt{p_{\rm succ}}}(\ln L_T)^{3/2}\right),\qquad L_T=\max(2,T_{\max}).$$
Repeating this finite amplified procedure $O(\ln(1/\rho))$ times gives success at least $1-\rho$ for $0<\rho<1/2$. The operation count is in the supplied stage-time metric; each controlled, inverse, reflection, preparation, and classical-construction cost remains explicit.

An unamplified attempt of degree $m$ uses exactly $m$ block-encoding signal calls in the QSVT sequence. Applying the supplied unknown-amplitude amplification procedure costs expected $O(m/\sqrt{p_{\rm impl}})$ signal calls, with state preparation, controlled/inverse calls, reflections, phase gates, synthesis, and classical certificate generation charged separately. When the degree theorem is established, $m=O(\delta^{-1}\ln(1/e))$, so this becomes $O(\delta^{-1}\ln(1/e)/\sqrt{p_{\rm impl}})$ expected signal calls, and the crude $\zeta\le\delta/4$ bound gives $O(\delta^{-2}\ln(1/e))$. This is an expected-cost statement; it does not assert a fixed worst-case stopping time.
